To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) we have defined a data model and a data structure able to support the integration of data from several sources and to provide a high level of data extensibility and (ii) we have implemented a repository based on this model, deployed on distributed resources and providing a simple and efficient web interface.
we have developed and implemented an extensible and distributed data model, which is based on a dynamic data structure, able to support multidisciplinary research experiments in neuroscience.

we have developed an extensible data model and structure that enables users to define their data types, to describe the processes and the events of their experiments, and to store and share their data on a distributed DataGrid.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a data model and a repository able to integrate data from different sources and to support multidisciplinary research.

the development of an innovative data model and structure for the storage and integration of data and metadata from different domains and with the development of a Grid-enabled repository for their management.
the definition of a dynamically extensible database model and its implementation as a distributed repository.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the proposed data model and repository can be considered a valuable and flexible tool to manage data in a collaborative multidisciplinary context, such as the neuroscientific one, where the data types to be handled are often not predefined.

the proposed data model, repository and web-based user interface represent a powerful tool to manage, store and share data in a distributed way, thus allowing to easily integrate and exploit data from different sources and to provide a common framework for multidisciplinary research and data sharing.

this work represents a first step towards the definition of a flexible and extensible data model for neuroscience research, able to support the integration of data from different sources and to provide a user-friendly interface for data management.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the data model has been defined and successfully tested, and that the repository has been deployed on distributed resources and used for a real case study.

the proposed data structure has been successfully implemented in a repository application, which is able to manage and integrate multimodal/multilevel data and metadata, providing an extensible environment for the development of new applications in neuroscience.

a dynamically extensible repository for data integration has been implemented and deployed, and that the repository has been used to manage multimodal and multiscale biomedical data for a large-scale clinical research project.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the data model and data structure we have implemented can be applied to a wide range of different applications in the field of neuroscience.

we have been able to build a data repository able to handle a large amount of data from heterogeneous sources, and to provide a user-friendly web interface to query, view and analyze the data in an integrated way.
it is possible to build a dynamically extensible and distributed repository for neuroscience data, which can be easily customized and extended by end users.
